messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 ALERT: Rapid GPU queue growth detected in us-west1-primary-gpu-pool. queue_length=124 (90p), tail_latency spikes, autoscaler attempted scale but failed with AllocationFailed/QUOTA_EXCEEDED. Possible cross-region spillover already happening to us-east1. https://redwood.internal/dashboards/queues#us-west1
Alex M: Ack, paging oncall. tagging SRE rotation. Can someone grab pager?
Shauna: I'm in. seeing lots of AllocationFailed entries in autoscaler logs:
```
2026-07-12T18:13:21Z ERROR AllocationFailed region=us-west1 reason=insufficient_accelerators details=GPUs-unavailable quota=project:GPUS=64 used=64
2026-07-12T18:13:24Z WARN AutoscalerRetry attempt=3 status=quotaExceeded
```
Shauna: autoscaler hit soft cap on project GPU quota. Also a subset of requests are getting 429 from the queue manager due to enforced throttle.
Jun: I'm taking pager. popping into the autoscaler controller now. quick check: any recent config changes to regional quotas or pool labels?
Alex M: No config deploys recently per deploy-bot, last was 2h ago. @deploy-bot can you confirm no config rollouts?
deploy-bot: No deploys to infra/autoscaler in last 6h.
Oliver: Oncall, I can work routing. current behavior: when us-west1 queue >50 we route a percentage to us-east1 as spillover. Looks like routing started at 18:12 but us-east1 pools are cold -> higher latency + some client timeouts.
Maria (CS): we already have one enterprise customer (CUST-42) reporting errors in their product flow — high 503s. They are on the us-west1 routing override. Please flag customer impact.
oncall-sre: Plan proposal: 1) Temporarily increase project GPU quota (if cloud allows) 2) Open controlled failover: increase spillover_ratio to 40% but prefer quantized-small variant to reduce cold KV penalty 3) Throttle non-critical background workloads (batch/async) 4) Notify CS + statuspage. Who can request quota bump?
Shauna: Tried quota API, cloud returned immediate denial. Looks like we already at org-level quota. Requesting cloud support now but ETA unknown.
Jun: While cloud support is pending, we can do immediate mitigations: - Update routing policy to prefer model-small-quant (lower memory) in spillover to decrease cold load - Pause async batch jobs tagged background=true across us-west1 - Increase circuit-breaker threshold to allow more in-flight for priority customers only
Oliver: I'm ready to push the routing change. pushing a canary to 10% -> monitor for errors. If stable, ramp to 40%.
Alex M: Do it. push commands and paste sha1. Keep ramp slow. Also add sticky header so session affinity for enterprise customers stays in us-west1 if they started there.
Oliver: Pushing policy patch now:
```bash
# routing policy patch
patch-routes --region=us-west1 --spillover-target=us-east1 --prefer-variant=model-small-quant --initial-rate=0.10 --ramp-to=0.40 --sticky-enterprise=true
```
Oliver: Canary pushed, waiting on metrics.
Shauna: Pausing batch workers in us-west1:
```bash
kubectl -n jobs patch cronjob batch-analytics -p '{"spec":{"suspend":true}}'
kubectl -n jobs label pods -l workload=background app=batch --overwrite batch-paused=true
```
Shauna: done, CPU/GPU pressure dropped ~8% already. queue_length down to 98 (18:18).
incident-bot: Metric update: queue_length(us-west1)=98 -> 76 over 6m after initial mitigations. downstream latency to enterprise customers improved from 2.8s -> 1.9s for routed traffic.
Maria (CS): Thanks team, I'm telling CUST-42 that we're doing targeted routing and throttling, ETA for stable fallback 30m. They asked for an RCA follow-up.
Jun: Cloud support still ETA>2h. Given quota denial, secondary mitigation: - Drain some preemptible pools in non-critical regions and temporarily move their GPUs to us-west1? Ops, that's messy and possibly not allowed. Thoughts?
Alex M: Do NOT move GPUs between regions. That's infra-level. Instead, can we enable queued request batching more aggressively for enterprise routes to reduce per-token GPU consumption?
Shauna: Increasing batching for enterprise only now (lower per-request overhead). Patch:
```yaml
route_overrides:
  enterprise-*-us-west1:
    max_batch_size: 64
    max_wait_ms: 40
```
Shauna: Applied. early signal: tokens/sec efficiency improved ~12%.
Oliver: Ramp to 40% spillover now.
incident-bot: Routing changed: spillover_ratio=0.40, prefer_variant=model-small-quant.
Jun: Monitoring SLOs. us-east1 latency is higher but error rate stable. us-west1 queue continues to decline.
Alex M: Quick customer-impact note for postmortem: affected customers: CUST-42 (partial outage), several small customers saw higher tail latency and transient 5xx. No data plane loss. Include timestamps and mitigation steps.
Maria (CS): I'm collecting affected customer list and will open support tickets for those impacted. keep me posted.
Shauna: Autoscaler logs now show reduced AllocationFailed errors; most requests being fulfilled via spillover + quantized variant. queue_length stabilized ~30.
Oliver: Rolling back the most aggressive throttles in 15m if trend holds.
Jun: Assigning follow-ups: - Shauna: postmortem for autoscaler failure + quota constraints - Oliver: routing policy playbook update to include prefer-variant option - Maria: customer communication and statuspage update - Alex M: coordinate with finance/cloud for quota increase request windows
Alex M: I’ll also open an incident ticket and assign severity P1->P1-brief (since impact limited and mitigations successful).
incident-bot: Incident created: INC-20260712-1962456789. Slack thread pinned. Paging rotation: Jun (current), Alex M (secondary).
Maria (CS): Posting initial status on statuspage now: "Partial degradation in us-west1 impacting subset of customers; mitigations in progress."
Alex M: Thanks all. keep one person on-watch for 1h, then re-evaluate. Great coordination. :thumbsup:
Shauna: on-watch for 60m. will update here if anything changes.
Jun: on-watch. closing pager handoff after 1h if stable.
incident-bot: Final metric snapshot at 1962457050: queue_length(us-west1)=18, spillover_ratio=0.40, errors reduced to baseline."
